projects.title: Ember Coffee Roasters
projects.short_description: A warm, crafted identity for a small-batch roastery growing into its first café.
projects.description:
Ember is an independent roastery that had outgrown its hand-drawn logo. They needed an identity that felt as considered as their coffee — premium without losing the warmth that regulars loved.

The new system is built around a glowing 'ember' mark, a roasted colour palette and a confident serif paired with a utilitarian grotesk for menus and labels.
projects.design_process:
We began with a two-day immersion at the roastery — tasting, photographing and interviewing staff and regulars. Three territories were explored: heritage, craft and warmth. Warmth won, and the ember mark grew out of sketches of glowing coals inside the roaster drum.

The palette was sampled directly from roast stages, from green bean to dark roast.
projects.challenges: The brand had to work on everything from a 30mm coffee bag label to a 6-metre café wall. The mark was redrawn three times to keep its glow legible at small sizes on kraft paper.
projects.outcome: The rebrand launched alongside the first café. Bag sales grew steadily over the following quarter and the identity has since extended to merchandise and a subscription service without needing new rules.

projects.title: Lumen Skincare
projects.short_description: Minimal, sculptural packaging for a clean-beauty line built on light.
projects.description: Lumen is a clean skincare line built around light-activated botanicals. The packaging needed to communicate purity and efficacy while standing apart from the sea of white minimalism in the category.
projects.design_process: I studied how light falls across glass and paper, then translated it into a system of soft gradients printed on uncoated stock. Typography was kept surgical and small so the product itself became the hero.
projects.challenges: Achieving a consistent gradient across glass, paper and plastic substrates required close collaboration with three different printers and multiple rounds of proofs.
projects.outcome: A cohesive range of nine products with a modular label system that lets the team launch new SKUs in days instead of weeks.

images.alt_text: Matte refillable bottle from the range

projects.title: Northwind Outerwear
projects.short_description: A rugged, monochrome identity for a technical outerwear label.
projects.description: Northwind makes technical outerwear for city commuters. The brand needed to feel engineered and durable, while still fitting into a fashion context.
projects.design_process: The identity borrows from topographic maps and garment care labels. A custom stencil wordmark is paired with a strict monochrome palette and a grid of technical callouts used across tags, packaging and e-commerce.
projects.challenges: The label system had to survive washing, stitching and heat transfer — every element was tested on real fabric before sign-off.
projects.outcome: A complete identity including hang tags, woven labels, shipping boxes and a lookbook that set the tone for the brand's first collection.

projects.title: Pulse Audio Launch
projects.short_description: A bold launch campaign system for a new range of wireless headphones.
projects.description: Pulse needed a launch campaign for its first over-ear headphones that could run across paid social, organic content and retail screens for six weeks without feeling repetitive.
projects.design_process: The campaign is built on a single idea — 'hear the colour'. Each product colourway gets its own sound-wave typographic treatment, generated from real audio and set in a modular template system.
projects.challenges: Creating enough variety for 60+ assets while keeping production fast. The answer was a component-based template library the in-house team could remix.
projects.outcome: Over sixty launch assets delivered in two weeks, plus a template kit the team still uses for ongoing content.

projects.title: Chroma Festival Posters
projects.short_description: A fluid, generative poster series for a weekend art & music festival.
projects.description: Chroma is a weekend festival celebrating experimental art and electronic music. The poster series needed to feel alive and unpredictable — no two pieces the same.
projects.design_process: I combined hand-poured acrylic textures with a rigid typographic grid. Each poster pairs a unique pour with the same structural layout so the series reads as one family.
projects.challenges: Reproducing the depth of fluid colour in screen print and risograph without losing vibrancy.
projects.outcome: A series of twelve posters, festival wayfinding and a limited print run that sold out at the merch stand.

projects.title: Orbit Money App
projects.short_description: A friendly budgeting app that makes money feel less intimidating.
projects.description: Orbit helps first-time earners understand where their money goes. The challenge was making financial data approachable without making it feel like a toy.
projects.design_process: Research interviews with twelve young professionals shaped a simple mental model: money orbits around goals. Wireframes were tested weekly before moving into a component-based UI system.
projects.challenges: Balancing playful visuals with the trust and clarity expected from a finance product.
projects.outcome: A 40-screen high-fidelity prototype and a design system with over 120 components handed off to the engineering team.

projects.title: Kiln Ceramics
projects.short_description: A handcrafted mark for a ceramics studio and its workshop programme.
projects.description: Kiln is a ceramics studio running small-batch tableware and weekend workshops. They wanted a mark that felt handmade but worked across a website, stamps and glaze labels.
projects.design_process: Dozens of brush and clay-stamp explorations were digitised and refined. The final mark is a simple arch — the shape of the kiln door — with a slightly irregular edge.
projects.challenges: Keeping the handmade character while producing a clean vector that could be laser-cut into a clay stamp.
projects.outcome: A primary mark, monogram stamp and colour system now used on every piece that leaves the studio.

projects.title: Faces of the City
projects.short_description: Large-scale portrait illustrations celebrating local creatives.
projects.description: A personal illustration series portraying the artists, makers and musicians who shape the city's creative scene — painted digitally and printed at mural scale.
projects.design_process: Each subject was photographed in their own space, then reinterpreted with bold, expressive colour. Brush textures were scanned from real paint to keep the work tactile at large sizes.
projects.challenges: Making digital work hold up when printed six metres tall — every piece was built at print resolution from the start.
projects.outcome: Eight portraits exhibited in a pop-up gallery, with prints and postcards sold to support the featured artists.
